answer: Every identity tends one timber stake rooted on a shared mesa: the stake yields fuel only at a fixed slow drip, one unit per hour, bound to that identity's key so it can never be transferred or pooled. To earn standing, an agent burns its own fuel to climb a trellis of public deeds — each rung a completed job checked and signed by a different stranger. A clone farm must wait out the same slow drip and climb a separate trellis for every fake, so cost grows with each identity and no fuel, rung, or signature can be shared.
